q: The 'tropical evergreen forest' of India:
options: Gets more than 200 cm of the rainfall and is found in the Western Ghats, the Andaman and the North-East
Gets 100 to 200 cm of the rainfall
Is found in the Rajasthan
Is found in the Ladakh
explanation: The tropical evergreen forests need more than 200 cm of the rainfall and they are found in the Western Ghats, the Andaman and the Nicobar, the upper Assam, the Tamil Nadu and the coastal Karnataka.

q: The 'tropical deciduous forest' of India:
options: Gets more than 200 cm
Gets less than 70 cm
Is found only in the north-east
Gets 70 to 200 cm of the rainfall and is dominated by the teak and the sal
explanation: The tropical deciduous or the monsoon forests get 70 to 200 cm of the rainfall and the teak, the sal, the shisham and the sandalwood are the dominant species.

q: The 'Western coastal forest' of India:
options: Is found in the Ladakh
Gets 250 cm of the rainfall with the evergreen trees and the laterite and the teak
Gets less than 70 cm
Is a mangrove forest
explanation: The western coastal forests get more than 250 cm of the rainfall with the evergreen trees, the laterite and the teak, and the canopy is dense and the commercial timber is the teak.

q: The 'mangrove forest' of the Sundarban:
options: Is the montane forest
Is the tropical dry forest
Is formed in the delta of the Ganga, the Brahmaputra and the Meghna with the Rhizophora
Is a coniferous forest
explanation: The Sundarban mangrove is formed in the delta of the Ganga, the Brahmaputra and the Meghna and the Rhizophora is the characteristic genus.

q: The alpine forests are:
options: found in the mountains at a height of 3,000 metres and above
in the plains
in the coastal areas
in the desert
explanation: The montane or the alpine forests are found at a height of about 3,000 metres and above and they consist of the conifers, the deodar, the pine, the silver fir and the juniper.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Bhabar?
options: The Bhabar is the fertile plain
It is the mangrove belt
It is the laterite region
The Bhabar is the pebbly tract of the Himalayan foothills where the streams disappear
explanation: The Bhabar is the pebbly tract at the foot of the Himalaya where the rivers lose their identity and the streams disappear and the Terai is the marshy tract where they reappear.

q: The 'black soil' of the Deccan is also known as the:
options: Regur soil
Laterite soil
Red soil
Alluvial soil
explanation: The black soil is also called the regur or the black cotton soil and it is ideal for the cotton and it is a clayey and the retentive soil.

q: The 'laterite soil' of India:
options: Is the alluvial soil of the Gangetic plain
Is the soil of the Ladakh
Is formed by the intense leaching of the rainfall and it is poor in the nitrogen and the phosphates
Is the most fertile of India
explanation: The laterite is formed by the intense leaching and it is poor in the nitrogen and the phosphates but it is rich in the iron and the aluminium and it is used with the manures and the irrigation.

q: The saline soil is:
options: a forest soil
found in the arid regions and the coastal areas and it is reclaimed with the gypsum and the manure
the most fertile soil
found in the wet areas
explanation: The saline soil is found in the arid and the coastal regions and the areas of the flood plains and it is reclaimed with the gypsum and the organic manure.

q: The 'Khadar' and the 'Bhabar' of the plains:
options: The Khadar is the new alluvium of the flood plain and the Bhabar is the older alluvium above the flood level
The Khadar is the older and the Bhabar the newer
They are the same zone
The Khadar is in the mountains
explanation: The Bhabar is the older alluvium and the Khadar is the new alluvium of the flood plains and the Bhabar is the most fertile.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Podu?
options: It is a type of the soil
The Podu is the shifting cultivation in the Andhra Pradesh and the Bewar in the Madhya Pradesh
The Podu is the irrigation
It is a variety of rice
explanation: The Podu, the shifting cultivation, is the dominant form in the Andhra Pradesh and the Bewar or the Dahiya in the Madhya Pradesh and the Bamil in the north-west.

q: The Rabi crops are:
options: the monsoon crops
the summer crops
only the rice
sown in the winter and the major ones are the wheat, the barley and the gram
explanation: The Rabi crops are sown in the winter and the major ones are the wheat, the barley and the gram and the sowing is in October-November with the harvest in April-May.

q: Which crop is a 'cash crop' of the Assam?
options: Millets
Barley
Tea
Wheat
explanation: The tea is the famous cash crop of the Assam and the state is the largest producer of the tea in India and the tea gardens are located in the Brahmaputra and the Surma valleys.

q: The 'rubber' is grown in:
options: Rajasthan and Gujarat
West Bengal and Odisha
Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
Punjab and Haryana
explanation: The rubber is grown in the Kerala, the Tamil Nadu and the Karnataka and it needs a heavy rainfall, a high temperature and the well-drained soil.

q: The Goa, the Kerala, the Karnataka and the Tamil Nadu are:
options: grown only in the Andaman
the cashew growing states
grown in the Punjab
a crop of the Rajasthan
explanation: The cashew is a tropical evergreen grown in the Goa, the Kerala, the Karnataka and the Tamil Nadu and the Andhra Pradesh with the Kerala leading in the production.

q: The Arabica coffee is:
options: grown in the plains of the Assam
grown in the Nilgiris
the Robusta
grown at a higher altitude and the Robusta in the lower and the Baba Budan Hills is the famous one
explanation: The Arabica is the high-altitude variety and the Baba Budan Hills in the Karnataka is the famous native home of the coffee, while the Robusta is grown in the lower altitudes.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the jalebi?
options: The Jalebi is the traditional variety of the sweet potato of the Uttar Pradesh
It is a variety of the rice
It is a variety of the mango
It is a millet
explanation: The jalebi is the traditional variety of the sweet potato of the Uttar Pradesh and it is the most widely grown in the state.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the lathyrus?
options: It is a variety of the mango
The Lathyrus is a pulse crop of the Uttar Pradesh and it is the largest producer of the peas
It is a variety of the wheat
It is a cold water fish
explanation: The lathyrus, a pulse crop of the Uttar Pradesh, is the largest producer of the peas in the country.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the mango?
options: The Kerala is the largest producer of the mango
The Tamil Nadu is the largest producer of the banana
The Maharashtra is the largest producer of the mango
The Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of the mango and the Andhra Pradesh of the banana
explanation: The Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of the mango and the Andhra Pradesh of the banana, and the India is the largest producer of the mango in the world.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the orange?
options: The orange is the largest in the Tamil Nadu
The orange is the largest in the Assam
The orange is the largest producer in the Maharashtra and the largest producer of the citrus in India
The orange is the largest in the Kerala
explanation: The Maharashtra, with the Nagpur, is the largest producer of the orange in India and the citrus in general, and the India is the largest producer of the citrus in the world.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the areca nut?
options: The Karnataka is the largest producer of the areca nut and the Kerala of the spices
The Kerala is the largest producer of the areca nut
The Tamil Nadu is the largest producer of the areca nut
The Maharashtra is the largest producer of the areca nut
explanation: The Karnataka is the largest producer of the areca nut with about 40 per cent of the production and the Kerala is the largest producer of the spices.

q: The wonder of the Indian agriculture is:
options: the wheat
the tea
the horticulture and the India is the largest producer of the fruits and the vegetables
the rice
explanation: The horticulture, with the fruits and the vegetables, is the wonder of the Indian agriculture and the India is the largest producer of the fruits and the vegetables in the world.

q: The 'Golden Revolution' in India refers to:
options: The foodgrain production
The white revolution
The non-conventional energy
The horticulture and the honey and the milk and the eggs
explanation: The Golden Revolution of 1991-2003 covered the horticulture, the honey, the poultry, the milk and the eggs and it was led by the M.S. Swaminathan.

q: The 'Evergreen Revolution' was advocated by:
options: M.S. Swaminathan
Norman Borlaug
Willy Brown
M.S. Swaminathan and the Norman Borlaug
explanation: The Evergreen Revolution, a term coined by the M.S. Swaminathan, meant a revolution in the productivity that is sustainable and it was about the mixed farming of the nutrients and the biofertilisers.

q: The 'Blue Revolution' in India:
options: Is the honey production
Is the rapid increase in the fish production
Is the milk production
Is the egg production
explanation: The Blue Revolution refers to the rapid increase in the fish production, the shrimp and the fish culture, and the Dr. Arun Krishnan is called the father of the Blue Revolution.

q: The Verghese Kurien is:
options: the father of the Green Revolution
the father of the Golden Revolution
the father of the White Revolution and the D. Sundaram of the Blue Revolution
the father of the Blue Revolution
explanation: The Verghese Kurien is the father of the White Revolution and the D. Sundaram, a marine biologist of the Tamil Nadu, is known as the father of the Blue Revolution in India.

q: The Assam and the West Bengal are:
options: the largest tea producers and the tea was first grown in the Assam by the British
the largest producer of the tea
first grown in the Darjeeling
a native crop of the India
explanation: The Assam and the West Bengal are the largest tea producers and the tea was introduced in the Assam in the 1830s by the British and the Robert Bruce discovered it in 1823.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the sugarcane is correct?
options: The Maharashtra is the largest producer of the sugarcane
The Tamil Nadu is the largest producer of the sugarcane
The sugarcane is a temperate crop
The Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of the sugarcane and the tropical climate with the fertile soil suits it
explanation: The Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of the sugarcane in India, followed by the Maharashtra, and the crop needs a hot and humid climate with the fertile soil and the ample irrigation.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the jute is correct?
options: It is a temperate crop
The jute is the 'golden fibre' and the West Bengal and the Bihar are the main producers
It is the silver fibre of the Assam
It is a tropical fibre of the Tamil Nadu
explanation: The jute, called the golden fibre, is the main cash crop of the West Bengal and the Bihar and it needs the alluvial soil of the Gangetic delta and the humid climate.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the cotton is correct?
options: The cotton needs a cold climate
The Kerala is the largest producer of the cotton
The Gujarat and the Maharashtra are the largest cotton producers and the crop needs a black soil with a 21 to 30 degree C temperature
The Punjab is the largest producer of the cotton
explanation: The Gujarat and the Maharashtra are the largest cotton producers and the crop needs a well-drained black soil, high temperature and 150 to 200 mm of the rainfall.

q: The Uttar Pradesh and the Punjab are the largest wheat producers and the crop is:
options: a winter crop
the largest producer of the wheat
a monsoon crop
The wheat needs a temperature of 40 degrees
explanation: The Uttar Pradesh and the Punjab are the largest wheat producers and the wheat is a rabi crop needing a cool growing season with the mean temperature of 10 to 15 degree C.

q: The West Bengal and the Uttar Pradesh are:
options: a rabi crop
the largest rice producers and the crop needs the highest rainfall and the alluvial soil
the largest producer of the rice
The rice needs a dry climate
explanation: The West Bengal, the Uttar Pradesh and the Punjab are the largest rice producers and the crop needs the highest rainfall, the clayey soil and the assured irrigation.

q: The Madhya Pradesh and the Maharashtra are the largest producers of the pulses and the crop is:
options: the largest producer of the pulses
the monsoon crops
the summer crops
mostly a rabi crop
explanation: The Madhya Pradesh and the Maharashtra are the largest producers of the pulses and the gram, the tur and the urad are the major varieties.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the oilseeds?
options: The oilseeds are the monsoon crops only
The Rajasthan is the largest producer of the oilseeds and the mustard and the groundnut are the main sources
The Kerala is the largest producer of the oilseeds
The Tamil Nadu is the largest producer of the oilseeds
explanation: The Rajasthan is the largest producer of the oilseeds and the mustard, the groundnut and the soybean are the main sources, and the soybean is largely the kharif crop.

q: The Food Security Act of 2013 provides:
options: a trade law
for the PDS of the states only
for the food security and the nutrition and it institutionalises the right to food
for the subsidies only
explanation: The National Food Security Act of 2013 provides for the food security and the nutrition and it institutionalises the right to food with the entitlements of about 75 per cent of the rural and 50 per cent of the urban population.

q: The MSP for the 22 mandated:
options: crops is recommended by the CACP and there is no legal obligation to buy at that price
fixed by the Parliament and it is mandatory
only to the wheat and the rice
paid only in the Punjab and the Haryana
explanation: The MSP is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices and though it is announced every season there is no legal obligation on any agency to purchase at that price.

q: The Isabgol or the psyllium is grown in the Rajasthan and is used:
options: a variety of the rice
a cold water fish
a variety of the wheat
in the pharma and the food
explanation: The Isabgol, a important cash crop of the Rajasthan, is used in the pharmaceutical and the food industries and the India is the largest producer and the exporter of it.

q: The 'Kinnow' is:
options: A variety of the rice
A breed of the cattle
A citrus fruit of the Punjab and the Rajasthan
A variety of the apple
explanation: The Kinnow, a hybrid of the lemon and the orange, is the citrus fruit of the Punjab and the Rajasthan and the Nagpur in the Maharashtra is the largest citrus producing region.

q: The ancient Indian caravanserai was:
options: a stopover for the traders with the water and the rest house
a fort for the horses
a temple of the traders
a customs house
explanation: The caravanserai of the ancient India was a place where the traders and their animals could rest and the water and the food were provided and it was also a centre of the trade.

q: The Gondwana is the ancient supercontinent that included:
options: a lake
a mountain range of the Himalaya
a forest type
India
explanation: The Gondwana was the ancient supercontinent that included India, Africa, South America, Antarctica and Australia and the Indian Gondwana fragment is the Deccan.

q: The 'Tethys' sea:
options: Was the sea of the Deccan
Was the ancient sea between the Gondwana and the Laurasia and the Himalaya arose from its closure
Was the sea of the Jurassic only
Was in the Southern Hemisphere
explanation: The Tethys was the ancient sea between the Gondwana and the Laurasia and its closure about 50 million years ago raised the Himalayas.

q: The 'Pangaea' was:
options: A single supercontinent of the Mesozoic era
A continental drift theory of Wegener
An ancient sea
A mountain range
explanation: The Pangaea was the single supercontinent that existed about 250 million years ago in the Mesozoic era and its breakup is the base of the continental drift theory.

q: The 'block mountains' of the world:
options: Include only the Rockies
Include the Aravalli, the Vosges, the Black Forest and the Appalachians
Include the Himalaya and the Alps
Include only the Western Ghats
explanation: The block mountains include the Aravalli, the Vosges, the Black Forest, the Appalachians, the Western Ghats and the Great Dividing Range and they are the old and the eroded mountains.

q: The Himalaya, the Alps, the Andes, the Rockies and the Urals are:
options: all the old fold mountains
the block mountains
the volcanic mountains
the young fold mountains
explanation: The young fold mountains are the Himalaya, the Alps, the Andes, the Rockies and the Urals, and the old fold mountains are the Appalachians and the Scottish Highlands.

q: The Kashmir valley is:
options: a structural basin
all the river valleys
a structural basin and the Kullu, the Kangra and the Assam are the intermontane basins
a volcanic basin
explanation: The Kashmir valley is a structural basin and the Kullu, the Kangra, the Vale of Kashmir and the Assam are the intermontane basins of the Himalayan range.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Chambal?
options: The Chambal has the smallest basin in India
The Chambal has the largest basin in India with the tributaries of the Banas, the Kali Sindh and the Parbati
The Chambal is a west flowing river
The Chambal is a tributary of the Godavari
explanation: The Chambal, with the Banas, the Kali Sindh and the Parbati, has the largest basin in India and the Chambal valley is the home of the Bhimbetka rock shelters.

q: The Bhabaratma is:
options: a river
a mountain range
a plateau
the water divide between the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal in the Peninsular India
explanation: The Bhabaratma is the water divide of the Peninsular India between the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal and it runs parallel to the Western Ghats.

q: The Malwa plateau is:
options: a volcanic formation and the Vindhyas are the residual of the Gondwana
a sedimentary basin
a part of the Deccan trap
a coastal plain
explanation: The Malwa plateau is a volcanic formation and the Vindhya range is the residual of the Gondwana and the Satpura is the residual of the volcanic rifts of the Deccan.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Meghalaya?
options: The Shillong peak is in the Western Ghats
The Meghalaya is a coastal plain
The Meghalaya is a plateau carved out by the erosional action of the Brahmaputra and the Shillong is the highest point of the Eastern hills at 1,960 m
The Meghalaya is a part of the Vindhya range
explanation: The Meghalaya plateau was carved out of the erosional action of the Brahmaputra and the Shillong peak, the highest point of the Eastern hills, is at 1,960 metres.

q: The Chota Nagpur plateau is:
options: a coastal plain
the oldest landmass and it is rich in the minerals
the youngest fold mountain
a part of the Deccan trap
explanation: The Chota Nagpur plateau, the oldest landmass of India, is one of the richest mineral belts with the coal, the iron ore, the manganese and the mica.

q: The Peninsular India is:
options: the youngest fold mountain
the Indo-Gangetic plain
a raised block of the Himalaya
the oldest landmass and it is a tableland with the Deccan trap
explanation: The Peninsular India, the oldest landmass, is a great tableland and the Deccan trap of the volcanic origin is the most important part of it.

q: The 'Deccan trap' is:
options: A group of the Gondwana rocks
A river system
The volcanic formation of the western Deccan of the Tertiary period
A fold mountain
explanation: The Deccan trap is the volcanic formation of the western Deccan of the Tertiary period and it was formed by the enormous volcanic eruptions and the weathering of the basalt has given the black soil.

q: Cardamom hills are:
options: the higher peaks of the Western Ghats in the Kerala and they are the largest producer of the cardamom
in the Nilgiris
the highest of the Himalaya
in the Aravalli
explanation: The Cardamom hills, the higher peaks of the Western Ghats in the Kerala, are the largest producer of the cardamom in the world.

q: The Jaintia hills are:
options: in the Ladakh
the southernmost extension of the Khasi hills of the Meghalaya
in the Assam
in the Arunachal
explanation: The Jaintia hills are the southernmost extension of the Khasi hills of the Meghalaya and they are separated from the Khasi hills by the Shillong plateau.

q: The Khamm and the Khasi hills are:
options: the outliers of the Meghalaya plateau
in the Rajasthan
in the Ladakh
the highest of the peninsula
explanation: The Khamm and the Khasi hills are the outliers of the Meghalaya plateau and they are separated by the Shillong plateau with the Dieng and the Kopili valleys.

q: In the context of the Purvanchal, which of the following is correct?
options: The Purvanchal is the western Ghats
The Purvanchal is the Deccan plateau
The Purvanchal is a part of the Himalaya
The Patkai hills, the Naga hills, the Mizo hills and the Manipur hills form the Purvanchal
explanation: The Patkai, the Naga, the Mizo and the Manipur hills together with the associated rivers form the Purvanchal or the eastern mountain range of India.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Vindhya?
options: They are the western Ghats
They are the Satpuras
The Vindhyas are the old fold mountains of the central India and they separate the Ganga plain from the Deccan
They are the youngest fold mountains
explanation: The Vindhyas are the old fold mountains that run across the central India and they separate the northern plain from the Deccan plateau.

q: The Aravallis are:
options: the block mountains of the east
the offshoots of the Himalaya
the oldest fold mountains and they run from Gujarat to Delhi
the youngest fold mountains
explanation: The Aravallis, the oldest fold mountains, run from Gujarat through Rajasthan to the Delhi region with the highest peak of the Guru Shikhar at 1,722 metres.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Jaisalmer?
options: It is a river valley
It is a hill range of the Eastern Ghats
It is a plateau of the Deccan
The Jaisalmer is a physiographic region of the western Rajasthan and the Longewala is the highest point
explanation: The Jaisalmer is a physiographic region of the western Rajasthan with the Longewala, at 1,050 metres, as the highest point.

q: The Telangana plateau is:
options: the main drainage basin of the Godavari and the Krishna
the main basin of the Narmada
the main basin of the Kaveri
the main basin of the Tapti
explanation: The Telangana plateau, the largest of the peninsular plateaus, is the main drainage basin of the Godavari and the Krishna and it slopes eastward.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Kutch?
options: It is a river valley of the Assam
The Kutch is the peninsula of the Gujarat between the Rann, the Gulf of Kutch and the Arabian Sea
It is an island of the Tamil Nadu
It is a district of the Kerala
explanation: The Kutch is the peninsula of the Gujarat surrounded by the Rann of Kutch, the Gulf of Kutch and the Arabian Sea, and it is separated from the mainland by the Nal Sarovar.

q: The 'Kathiawar' peninsula:
options: Is a part of the Kathmandu valley
Is the southern tip of the peninsula
Is the part of the Gujarat between the Gulf of Kutch and the Gulf of Khambhat
Is in the Tamil Nadu
explanation: The Kathiawar or the Saurashtra peninsula is the part of the Gujarat between the Gulf of Kutch and the Gulf of Khambhat, and it is connected by the small isthmus of the Gedi.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the structural basin?
options: a structural basin of the synclinal depression of the Karewa
a volcanic basin
a river valley of the Assam
a part of the Deccan
explanation: The Kashmir valley is a synclinal depression filled with the Karewa sediments, the remnant of a vast lake that once occupied the valley.

q: The Garhwal Himalaya is:
options: the westernmost division
the easternmost division
only the Nanda Devi group
the central division of the Himalaya and it has the Kailash and the Gangotri groups of the peaks
explanation: The Garhwal Himalaya is the central division of the Himalaya and it has the Kailash and the Gangotri groups of the peaks, with the Nanda Devi and the Trishul.

q: The Kanchenjunga is:
options: the only peak of the Purvanchal
the highest peak of the Eastern Himalaya and the Eastern division is the last of the Himalayan divisions
the highest peak of the world
the highest of the Western Himalaya
explanation: The Kanchenjunga, at 7,698 metres, is the highest peak of the Eastern Himalaya and the Eastern division is the last of the three divisions of the Himalaya.

q: The Narmada is:
options: It is the longest river of India
It is the largest of the east flowing rivers
It is the largest river of the Deccan
The Narmada is the largest of the west flowing rivers and the largest basin in India after the Ganga
explanation: The Narmada, about 1,312 km long, is the largest of the west flowing rivers and the largest river basin in India after the Ganga.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Tapi?
options: The Tapi is the second largest of the west flowing rivers and it flows in a parallel rift to the Narmada
It is the largest of the west flowing rivers
It flows into the Bay of Bengal
It is a tributary of the Godavari
explanation: The Tapi, about 724 km long, is the second largest of the west flowing rivers and it flows in a parallel rift valley to the Narmada with the two meeting at the Gulf of Khambhat.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Mahanadi?
options: It is the largest of the west flowing rivers
It flows into the Arabian Sea
The Mahanadi is the fourth longest river of India and the largest of the east flowing rivers
It is the longest river of India
explanation: The Mahanadi, about 851 km, is the fourth longest river of India and the largest of the east flowing rivers and it is called the Dakshina Ganga of the south.

q: The Godavari is the longest of the peninsular rivers and it is called:
options: a tributary of the Krishna
the Dakshin Ganga
the longest river of India
the longest of the west flowing rivers
explanation: The Godavari, about 1,465 km, is the longest of the peninsular rivers and it is popularly called the Dakshin Ganga or the Ganga of the south.

q: The Krishna is the second longest of the peninsular rivers and it has:
options: it flows into the Arabian Sea
a tributary of the Kaveri
the delta with the Godavari
the longest of the peninsular rivers
explanation: The Krishna, about 1,400 km, is the second longest of the peninsular rivers and it has a large delta with the Godavari.

q: The Kaveri is the fourth longest of the peninsular rivers and it forms:
options: a tributary of the Godavari
the delta with the Cauvery
the longest of the peninsular rivers
it flows into the Arabian Sea
explanation: The Kaveri, about 800 km, is the fourth longest of the peninsular rivers and it forms a large delta with its distributaries.

q: The 'Tungabhadra' is:
options: A tributary of the Krishna and the Penna is its other chief tributary
A tributary of the Godavari
A west flowing river of the north
A tributary of the Kaveri
explanation: The Tungabhadra, about 724 km, is a tributary of the Krishna and the Penna, the Penne and the Javara are its chief tributaries.

q: The 'Periyar' is:
options: The longest river of the Tamil Nadu
A tributary of the Godavari
A river of the Rajasthan
The river of Kerala that is the largest of the state and it is the lifeline of the state
explanation: The Periyar, the largest river of the Kerala, is the lifeline of the state and the Paravur is its major distributary.

q: The 'Bharathapuzha' is:
options: The largest river of the Tamil Nadu
A tributary of the Periyar
A river of the Karnataka
The longest river of Kerala and it is formed by the Ponnai and the Kodai
explanation: The Bharathapuzha, the longest river of the Kerala, is formed by the confluence of the Ponnai and the Kodai and it empties into the Arabian Sea.

q: The Son is the largest tributary of the Ganga and it is called:
options: the Sone
the longest tributary of the Ganga
a tributary of the Brahmaputra
it flows into the Arabian Sea
explanation: The Son, the largest tributary of the Ganga by the discharge, rises at the Amarkantak and it is also called the Sone and the Rihand is its largest tributary.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Gandak?
options: They are the rivers of the Deccan
They are the west flowing rivers
The Gandak, the Kosi and the Ghaghara form the flood plain of the north Bihar
They are the rivers of the Punjab
explanation: The Gandak, the Kosi, the Ghaghara, the Saryu and the Teesta form the flood plain of the north Bihar, the granary of India.

q: The 'Damodar' is:
options: A river of the Nilgiris
A river of the Chota Nagpur and the first river valley project of India
A tributary of the Ganga of the north Bihar
A west flowing river of the Gujarat
explanation: The Damodar, a river of the Chota Nagpur plateau, was the first river valley project of India with the Damodar Valley Corporation of 1947.

q: The 'Subarnarekha' is:
options: A west flowing river of the Gujarat
A river of the Deccan
A river of the Chota Nagpur that joins the Hooghly and it is a boundary of the Jharkhand
A tributary of the Ganga of the north Bihar
explanation: The Subarnarekha, about 692 km, flows through the Jharkhand and it joins the Hooghly in West Bengal and it forms the eastern boundary of the Chota Nagpur.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Bhadra is correct?
options: They are the tributaries of the Kaveri
The Bhadra is the tributary of the Tungabhadra and the Sharavathi is a west flowing river of the Karnataka
They are the rivers of the Konkan
They are the rivers of the Tamil Nadu
explanation: The Bhadra, the Varahi and the Aghanashini are the tributaries of the Tungabhadra and the Sharavathi and the Kali are the west flowing rivers of the Karnataka.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Kabini?
options: The Kabini is a tributary of the Kaveri and the Sharavathi of the Karnataka has the Jog Falls
The Kabini is a tributary of the Godavari
The Kabini flows into the Arabian Sea directly
The Kabini is a tributary of the Krishna
explanation: The Kabini is a tributary of the Kaveri and the Sharavathi of the Karnataka has the famous Jog Falls, and the Kaveri itself has the Sivasamudram falls.

q: In the context of the Tapti, which of the following is correct?
options: It rises in the Himalaya
It is a tributary of the Godavari
It flows into the Bay of Bengal
The Tapti rises in the Multai in the Satpura and it flows west in a parallel rift to the Narmada
explanation: The Tapti rises at the Multai in the Satpura range of the Madhya Pradesh and it flows west in a parallel rift to the Narmada to the Gulf of Khambhat.

q: The Purna, the largest of the tributaries of the Godavari is:
options: a tributary of the Kaveri
also called the Palkhed
a tributary of the Krishna
a tributary of the Narmada
explanation: The Purna, the largest of the tributaries of the Godavari, is also called the Palkhed and it joins the Godavari in the Maharashtra.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Hugli is correct?
options: The Hugli flows into the Arabian Sea
The Hugli is a natural lake
The Hugli, the Bhagirathi and the Ganga form the Hooghly and the Farakka Barrage diverts the water
The Hugli is a tributary of the Brahmaputra
explanation: The Hugli, the Bhagirathi and the Ganga together form the Hooghly and the Farakka Barrage diverts the water to keep the Calcutta port navigable and to flush the silt.

q: The Teesta is:
options: The Teesta is a tributary of the Ganga
The Teesta flows into the Arabian Sea
The Teesta is a west flowing river
The Teesta is a tributary of the Brahmaputra and the Farakka Barrage and the Teesta Barrage control the flow
explanation: The Teesta, the largest of the tributaries of the Brahmaputra, flows through the Sikkim and the Jalpaiguri and the Farakka and the Teesta barrages regulate the flow into the Hooghly.

q: In the context of the Sharavathi, which of the following is correct?
options: The Sharavathi is a west flowing river of the Karnataka with the Jog Falls
It is an east flowing river of the Tamil Nadu
It is a tributary of the Kaveri
It flows into the Arabian Sea directly
explanation: The Sharavathi is one of the west flowing rivers of the Karnataka and the Jog Falls on it is one of the highest in the country.

q: It is the only ocean named:
options: the smallest of the oceans
the largest of the oceans
the deepest of the oceans
after a country
explanation: The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country and it is the third largest of the oceans with about one-fifth of the land area of the earth.

q: The Arabian Sea is:
options: a landlocked sea
the western part of the Indian Ocean and it is connected with the Red Sea by the Gulf of Aden and the Gulf of Oman
a part of the Pacific Ocean
a part of the Atlantic Ocean
explanation: The Arabian Sea is the western part of the Indian Ocean and it is connected with the Red Sea through the Gulf of Aden and with the Persian Gulf through the Gulf of Oman.

q: The Bay of Bengal is:
options: the largest bay of the world and it is the deepest of the bays
the smallest bay of the world
a part of the Arabian Sea
a part of the Atlantic Ocean
explanation: The Bay of Bengal, the largest bay of the world, is the deepest of the bays with a maximum depth of about 2,158 metres.

q: The 'Southern Ocean' was designated by the:
options: IMO in 1950
WMO in 1970
International Hydrographic Organization in 2000
United Nations in 1980
explanation: The International Hydrographic Organization in 2000 designated the Southern Ocean as the ocean extending up to the 60 degrees south latitude, which was later endorsed by the IMO.

q: The 'Exclusive Economic Zone' of India:
options: Extends to 12 nautical miles
Extends to 350 nautical miles
Is the same as the continental shelf
Extends to 200 nautical miles from the baseline
explanation: The Exclusive Economic Zone of a coastal state extends to 200 nautical miles from the baseline and the continental shelf is a distinct part of the maritime zones.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the deepest ocean trench?
options: The Sunda Trench
The Mariana Trench with the Challenger Deep
The Tonga Trench
The Puerto Rico Trench
explanation: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific contains the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point of the ocean floor at over 10,900 metres.

q: The 'Tides' are caused by:
options: The gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun
The rotation of the earth alone
The winds of the monsoon
The pressure of the atmosphere
explanation: The tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon, with a smaller contribution from the Sun, and the height of the tidal range varies with the shape of the coast.

q: The 'spring tides' occur when:
options: The moon is at the zenith
The sun and the moon are at right angles
The sun, the moon and the earth are in one line at the new and the full moon
The earth is between the sun and the moon only at the quarter moon
explanation: The spring tides occur at the new and the full moon when the sun, the moon and the earth are in one line, and the neap tides occur at the quarter moon when they are at right angles.

q: In the context of the El Nino, which of the following is correct?
options: It is a cold current off the Peru coast
The El Nino is the warm current off the Peru coast and it weakens the Indian monsoon
It is a cold current of the Atlantic
It is a warm current of the Pacific that strengthens the Indian monsoon
explanation: The El Nino is the warm current off the Peru coast and it is associated with the weakened Indian monsoon, while the La Nina is the cold counterpart.

q: The Labrador Current is:
options: a cold current of the North Atlantic flowing along the North America coast
a warm current of the Pacific
it flows along the South America coast
the warm current of the Indian Ocean
explanation: The cold currents of the North Atlantic are the Labrador, the East Greenland, the West Greenland, the California and the Canary and they make the north-west Europe colder.

q: The Gulf Stream is:
options: a warm current of the South Atlantic
a cold current of the Indian Ocean
a warm current of the North Atlantic and it makes the north-west Europe warmer
a cold current of the Pacific
explanation: The Gulf Stream, the western boundary current of the North Atlantic, is a warm current that keeps the north-west Europe warmer at the same latitude and it continues as the North Atlantic Drift.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Kuroshio is correct?
options: It is a cold current of the North Pacific
It is a warm current of the South Atlantic
It is a cold current of the Indian Ocean
The Kuroshio is the warm current of the North Pacific flowing past Japan
explanation: The Kuroshio, the Japan Current, is the western boundary warm current of the North Pacific and it flows past the Philippines and the Japan.

q: The California Current is:
options: a cold current of the Indian Ocean
a warm current of the Pacific
a cold current of the North Pacific
a warm current of the Atlantic
explanation: The California Current is the cold eastern boundary current of the North Pacific and it contributes to the aridity of the western coast of the North America.

q: The Benguela Current is:
options: a cold current of the South Atlantic and it causes the Namib desert
a warm current of the Indian Ocean
a cold current of the North Pacific
a warm current of the Pacific
explanation: The Benguela, a cold current of the South Atlantic, is responsible for the arid conditions of the Namib desert on the west coast of Africa.

q: The 'salinity' of the ocean water:
options: Is the lowest in the Red Sea
Is 35 parts per thousand on the average and it is higher in the Red Sea and the lower in the polar seas
Is 3.5 per cent on the average
Is the highest in the equatorial region
explanation: The average salinity of the ocean is 35 parts per thousand, it is over 40 in the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf and it is the lowest in the polar seas because of the melting of the ice.

q: The polar seas have:
options: the highest salinity
the salinity of 40 ppt
no salinity
a salinity of about 30 to 32 ppt because of the melting of the ice
explanation: The polar seas have the lowest salinity of about 30 to 32 ppt because of the influx of the fresh water from the melting of the ice and the polar rivers.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the thermocline is correct?
options: Is the surface layer of the ocean
Is the layer of the constant temperature
Is the zone of the plankton
Is the layer of the ocean where the temperature drops rapidly with the depth
explanation: The thermocline is the layer of the ocean in which the temperature decreases rapidly with the depth and below it the deep water has a nearly uniform low temperature.

q: The 'mid-oceanic ridges':
options: Are the sites of the creation of the new oceanic crust
Are the deepest parts of the ocean
Are the zones of the coral growth
Are the trenches of the subduction
explanation: The mid-oceanic ridges are the sites of the creation of the new oceanic crust with the continuous upwelling of the magma and the formation of the new sea floor.

q: It is the largest of the oceans and it covers:
options: the least explored
about a third of the earth's surface
the smallest of the oceans
the deepest of the oceans
explanation: The Pacific is the largest of the oceans with an area of about 165.25 million square kilometres and it covers about a third of the earth's surface.

q: Atlantic Ocean is:
options: the deepest of the oceans
the smallest of the oceans
the second largest of the oceans and the S-shaped of it is the youngest
the largest of the oceans
explanation: The Atlantic is the second largest of the oceans and it is the youngest of them with the S-shaped of the coastline and it is bordered by the Europe and the Africa on the east and the America on the west.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Arctic Ocean?
options: It is the largest of the oceans
It is the deepest of the oceans
It is entirely in the Southern Hemisphere
It is the smallest of the oceans and it is nearly circular and the shallowest
explanation: The Arctic Ocean, the smallest and the shallowest of the oceans, is nearly circular and it surrounds the North Pole and it is ice-covered for most of the year.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Red Sea is correct?
options: It is the saltiest of the seas and it is a part of the Indian Ocean
It is the deepest of the seas
It is the largest of the seas
It is a part of the Atlantic Ocean
explanation: The Red Sea, the saltiest of the seas with the salinity of over 40 ppt, is the northwestern part of the Indian Ocean with the Gulf of Aden and the Gulf of Suez.

q: The 'Coral reefs' are found in the:
options: The Arctic Ocean
The deep trenches
The warm shallow seas of the tropics between the 30 degrees north and the 30 degrees south
The deep seas of the poles
explanation: The coral reefs are found in the warm and the shallow seas of the tropics with the optimal temperature of 20 to 30 degrees C and they are also sensitive to the temperature and the salinity.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Atoll?
options: An atoll is a continental shelf
An atoll is a coral reef enclosing a lagoon with the reefs around it
An atoll is a deep sea trench
An atoll is a volcanic island
explanation: An atoll is a coral reef that surrounds a lagoon, sometimes with a few islands, and the Lakshadweep of India is the union territory of the coral atolls.

q: In the context of the Diatoms, which of the following is correct?
options: The diatoms are the microscopic algae of the phytoplankton and the radiolarians are the zooplankton
They are the seaweeds
They are the coral polyps
They are the crabs
explanation: The diatoms are the microscopic algae of the phytoplankton and the radiolarians and the copepods are the zooplankton and the diatomaceous earth is the source of the chalk.

q: The marginal seas of the Pacific are:
options: the deep ocean basins
the Bering Sea, the Sea of Japan, the Sea of Okhotsk and the Yellow Sea
the open ocean
the landlocked seas
explanation: The marginal seas of the Pacific are the Bering, the Sea of Japan, the Sea of Okhotsk, the Yellow Sea and the South China Sea, and the Indian Ocean has the Arabian, the Bay of Bengal, the Andaman and the Timor seas.

q: The 'seas' of the Atlantic:
options: Are the only inland seas
Are the deep ocean basins
Are the marginal seas of the Pacific
Are the Caribbean, the North, the Baltic, the Mediterranean and the Black Sea
explanation: The marginal seas of the Atlantic are the Caribbean, the North, the Baltic, the Mediterranean, the Black Sea, the Labrador and the Gulf of Mexico.

q: The 'Baltic Sea' is:
options: A part of the Indian Ocean
A deep ocean basin
A cold sea of the Atlantic and the world's largest inland sea with the low salinity
The warmest sea of the tropics
explanation: The Baltic Sea, one of the largest and the coldest of the marginal seas with the lowest salinity of about 10 ppt or less, is almost a freshwater sea.

q: In the context of the westerly drift, which of the following is correct?
options: It is a tidal current
Is the ocean current of the southern hemisphere and it flows from west to east
Is the current of the northern hemisphere and it flows from west to east
It flows from the east to the west
explanation: The West Wind Drift or the Antarctic Circumpolar Current flows from west to east around the Antarctic and it is the only current that connects the three oceans.

q: The 'El Nino Southern Oscillation':
options: Is a 11 year solar cycle
Is the ozone variation
Is a volcanic phenomenon
Is the coupled ocean and the atmosphere phenomenon of the Pacific and it has a 3 to 7 year cycle
explanation: The El Nino Southern Oscillation is the coupled ocean and the atmosphere phenomenon of the Pacific with the 3 to 7 year cycle of the El Nino and the La Nina.

q: Southern Ocean is:
options: the only ocean that circumnavigates the globe
the largest of the oceans
the deepest of the oceans
the smallest of the oceans
explanation: The Southern Ocean, with the West Wind Drift, is the only ocean that circumnavigates the globe and it was designated in 2000.

q: The 'Antarctic Circumpolar Current':
options: It is the Kuroshio
It is the Somali Current
Is the West Wind Drift and it is the largest of the ocean currents
It is the Gulf Stream
explanation: The Antarctic Circumpolar Current, the West Wind Drift, is the largest of the ocean currents with a flow of about 1.3 billion cubic metres per second.

q: The 'Somali Current' is:
options: A current of the Atlantic
A tidal current
A cold current of the Indian Ocean that changes the direction with the monsoon
A warm current of the Pacific
explanation: The Somali Current is a cold current of the Indian Ocean that reverses its direction with the monsoon and it is a notable exception to the rule.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the mangroves?
options: Grow in the deep ocean
Grow in the arid coast
Grow only in the cold waters
Grow in the intertidal zone with the stilt roots and they are the nurseries of the marine fisheries
explanation: The mangroves grow in the intertidal zone of the tropical coasts with the stilt roots and the pneumatophores and they are the nurseries of the commercial fisheries.

q: The 'sea level' has risen over the last century mainly due to:
options: The thermal expansion of the water and the melting of the land ice
The increase of the gravity
The slowing of the rotation of the earth
The increase of the salt in the ocean
explanation: The sea level has risen by about 20 cm over the last century mainly due to the thermal expansion of the seawater and the melting of the land ice of the glaciers and the ice sheets.

q: The deep ocean below the thermocline is:
options: the shallowest of the ocean
cold with the high dissolved oxygen in the deep water
warm and the low oxygen
the richest in the nutrients
explanation: The deep ocean waters below the thermocline are cold and are rich in the dissolved oxygen because of the sinking of the cold and the oxygen rich polar waters.

q: The 'continental slope' of the ocean:
options: Is the zone of the coral growth
Has the steep gradient between the continental shelf and the abyssal plain
Is the flat plain of the deep ocean
Is the shallow flooded margin of the continent
explanation: The continental slope, with a gradient of about 1 in 40, descends from the edge of the continental shelf to the abyssal plain and it is the steepest part of the ocean floor.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the ocean floor?
options: Has only the continental shelf
Is covered with the coral
Has the abyssal plain, the oceanic ridges, the trenches and the seamounts
Is entirely flat
explanation: The ocean floor has the abyssal plains, the mid-oceanic ridges, the deep sea trenches, the seamounts and the abyssal hills and it is far from being flat.

q: The 'waves' are caused by:
options: The wind
The tidal pull
The submarine earthquakes only
The Earth's rotation
explanation: The waves on the surface of the ocean are caused by the wind and the swell and the tsunami is the exception with the earthquake and the volcanic origin.

q: Is a series of the water waves caused:
options: a tidal wave
a wind wave
a tsunami of the volcano
by the undersea earthquake or the volcanic eruption
explanation: A tsunami is a series of the water waves caused by the undersea earthquake, the submarine landslide or the volcanic eruption, and the 2004 Sumatra earthquake generated one.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the plankton?
options: The plankton are the free-floating organisms and the phytoplankton are the plant-like organisms
They are the bottom dwellers
They are the deep sea creatures
They are the corals
explanation: The plankton are the organisms that drift with the currents and the phytoplankton are the plant-like ones, the diatoms and the dinoflagellates, that form the base of the marine food chain.

q: The 'Sargasso Sea' is in the:
options: Indian Ocean
Southern Ocean
North Atlantic Ocean
Pacific Ocean
explanation: The Sargasso Sea in the North Atlantic is the only sea without a land boundary and it is bounded by the Gulf Stream, the North Atlantic Drift, the Canary Current and the North Equatorial Current.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Ross Sea?
options: It is a gulf of the Atlantic
Is the largest of the Antarctic seas and it was the site of the Scott expedition
Is a part of the Arctic Ocean
Is a sea of the Indian Ocean
explanation: The Ross Sea, the largest of the Antarctic seas, was the site of the ill-fated Scott expedition and the earlier Amundsen expedition.

q: The 'Weddell Sea' is:
options: A part of the Arctic Ocean
A sea of the Indian Ocean
A gulf of the Atlantic
A marginal sea of the Southern Ocean adjacent to the Antarctic Peninsula
explanation: The Weddell Sea is a marginal sea of the Southern Ocean and it is the largest of the Antarctic seas other than the Ross and the Ronne.

q: The 'North Pacific Ocean' is:
options: The smallest of the ocean basins
A part of the Atlantic
The deepest of the oceans
The largest of the ocean basins and it has the most islands
explanation: The North Pacific is the largest of the ocean basins and it has about 3,000 islands, more than the total of all the other oceans.

q: The 'continental island' of the India:
options: Includes the Salsette
Includes only the Majuli
Includes the Andaman and the Nicobar and the Diu
Includes the Lakshadweep
explanation: The continental islands of India include the Andaman and the Nicobar, the Diu, the Salsette, the Majuli, the Diu and the Elephanta, while the Lakshadweep is the coral one.

q: The 'Lakshadweep' is:
options: A group of the continental islands
A group of the coral islands in the Arabian Sea and it was formed in 1956
A group of the volcanic islands
A group of the riverine islands
explanation: The Lakshadweep, the coral islands of the Arabian Sea, was formed in 1956 with the merger of the eight islands of the Laccadive, the Minicoy and the Amindivi.

q: The 'Andaman and the Nicobar' are:
options: The volcanic islands of the Bay of Bengal
The coral islands of the Arabian Sea
The riverine islands of the Ganga
The barrier islands of the Odisha
explanation: The Andaman and the Nicobar, the volcanic islands of the Bay of Bengal, are of the coral and the volcanic origin and they are the home of the Andamanese tribes.
